title: SensOFormer: Foundation Models for Particle Accelerators
claim: A single self-supervised encoder-processor-decoder model, pretrained by masked denoising, is reused with light task heads across diverse downstream tasks.
layout: 3 stacked panels, top-to-bottom; color-coded module diagrams with tensor shapes on arrows
description: The figure has three stacked panels. Panel (a) shows pretraining with four small grids of sensors against time, each with purple cells marking a different mask type: point-wise, time-wise, channel-wise and block-wise. A legend notes random mask type and random noise on unmasked points. Panel (b) is the largest and is split into three sub-diagrams of left-to-right boxes and arrows with tensor shapes such as (BL,C,d). The pink set encoder uses channel tokenization, latent-slot queries and cross-attention. The grey latent transformer processor has self-attention, add and norm, feed forward and an Nx repeat. The green set decoder uses cross-attention, layer norm and projection. Panel (c) shows three downstream tasks. Each pairs a frozen E and P block with a trained task head D1, D2 or D3, marked by snowflake and flame icons.
caption: Overview of SensOFormer. (a) Self-supervised pretraining uses masked denoising reconstruction. A mask is sampled from a mask bank containing point-wise, time-wise, channel-wise, and block-wise masks, while noise is added to the unmasked values. (b) SensOFormer uses an encoder--processor--decoder architecture for variable sensor sets. The perceiver-style set encoder is permutation-invariant across sensor channels. The latent transformer processor models temporal dependencies. The set decoder is permutation-equivariant, producing channel-wise reconstructions that preserve the queried sensor identities. (c) The pretrained encoder--processor backbone is reused with task-specific heads for missing-data imputation, anomaly detection, and cavity/fault identification.
abstract: Large-scale scientific facilities, such as particle accelerators, are complex systems composed of thousands of interacting components that must operate collectively to support diagnostics and control, and ensure safe, reliable operation. These facilities rely on extensive sensor networks that generate large volumes of heterogeneous, incomplete, and noisy telemetry, often sampled at different rates across subsystems. In this paper, we adopt the foundation-model paradigm to learn general-purpose sensor representations from historical accelerator data through self-supervised pretraining. We introduce SensOFormer, a denoising masked transformer with a Perceiver-style encoder-decoder architecture designed to handle variable sensor sets, accommodate heterogeneous sampling rates, and learn robust representations from noisy measurements. The model is pretrained on multiple particle-accelerator datasets and transferred to downstream tasks, including missing-data imputation, anomaly detection, cavity identification, and fault identification. Through extensive evaluations and comparisons, we demonstrate that a single self-supervised model can learn reusable representations for diverse operational tasks in large-scale scientific facilities. Project page: https://mahindrautela.github.io/sensoformer.
